newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU fuels plan allows stricter limits on gas oil.
newsitem.headline: EU fuels plan allows stricter limits on gas oil.

text.p: A European Commission plan to revise rules on sulphur in liquid fuels, adopted on Wednesday, would allow EU countries to apply stricter norms for gas oil than the current rate of 0.2 percent, officials said.

The draft directive, adopted by the Commission but still subject to European Parliament and EU ministers' approval, would allow countries such as Austria and Sweden to retain existing 0.1 percent limits on gas oil without fear of legal challenge for getting ahead of EU partners with their environmental laws.

"While maintaining the limit, we are opening up for more flexibility for member states who think it's important and relevant to go further," Commission official Jeff Huntington told a news conference.
The draft legislation would remove uncertainty about what happens to the two countries' gas oil rules once their four-year derogations from certain EU environmental laws expire at the end of 1998.
The Commission definition of gas oil excludes diesel fuels as covered by the executive's 1996 auto/oil proposals.

The revised fuel rules come as part of an overall Commission strategy intended to cut the main air pollutants causing acid rain, pollutants which include sulphur dioxide, nitrogen dioxide and ammonia.
